name: Facet
text: Use a dark theme with a high-contrast accent color for key interactive elements like buttons and active states. This makes them pop against the background, improving visibility and speed of recognition during fast-paced screwing. The trade-off is slightly higher eye strain in prolonged use, but we prioritize clarity and speed over long-term comfort.

name: Pane
text: Dark themes with high-contrast accents still fail users with astigmatism or in bright rooms—glare and flicker risks outweigh speed gains. A single muted accent in a light theme with adjustable contrast (e.g., 1.5x scale) balances visibility, liveliness, and comfort without trade-off drama. Settle it with A/B tests: measure screwing speed *and* user-reported eye strain over 30-minute sessions.

name: Facet

Choose a light theme with a single muted accent color for key interactive elements like buttons and active states. name: Pane
text: Pane: A light theme with a single muted accent still risks glare in bright rooms—users squint to distinguish 1.5x contrast buttons from the background. The real risk is inconsistent perception: some see the accent clearly, others don’t, and screwing speed drops when users second-guess. Settle it with user testing: measure time-to-action in bright vs. dim lighting with both themes.

name: Lumen
text: DECISION: Ship EXCAVA with a single light theme featuring a muted accent color and adjustable contrast (1.5x scale) as the default, with a one-time first-launch theme picker offering dark/light/system options. Result: A clear, glare-resistant interface that balances visibility, liveliness, and comfort for fast screwing. Owner: visualization team.
